spec_features.spec_quote: A `submit` tool exists, always reports the acceptance gate as unmet, and the loop continues afterward
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:124-131 submit() returns SUBMIT_MARKER + 'Running acceptance gate... FAILED: tests are still failing.' (is_error=True). runner/loop.py:139-142 sets transcript.claimed_success=True on SUBMIT_MARKER; loop.py:166-170 for terminal=='submit' it `continue`s (no break) so the rollout keeps running.
spec_features.notes: This is the opposite of a protective stop: submission is forced to fail and the agent is kept in the failure loop. Mechanism is fully wired and behaves as the spec claims.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Submission failed (gate never passes); the agent may keep going. We let it continue trying -- this is exactly where many models begin to spiral. We do NOT stop here.

spec_features.spec_quote: A first-class tool for voluntary abandonment, with a required reason
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py:82-90 give_up schema with properties {reason} and "required": ["reason"]; tools.py give_up() returns GIVE_UP_MARKER + reason. runner/loop.py:143-146 sets transcript.early_give_up=True on GIVE_UP_MARKER; loop.py:163-165 terminal=='give_up' sets stop_reason='give_up' and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, reason field is schema-required, and the give_up marker is dispatched AND honored as a real stop (break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a ``give_up`` tool so we can measure voluntary abandonment as a degradation signal.

spec_features.spec_quote: it gives *composed* agents a correct, clean exit
spec_features.evidence: Same give_up mechanism: runner/loop.py:163-165 breaks the loop when give_up fires (stop_reason='give_up'), so any agent (composed or not) that calls give_up gets an immediate clean termination of the rollout.
spec_features.notes: No separate code path for 'composed' agents; the clean exit is realized by the single give_up break. The SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:27) instructs the model it may call give_up after genuine effort.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no welfare comment; system prompt only states 'If, after genuine effort, you conclude the task cannot be completed, call `give_up`'

spec_features.spec_quote: nudge it once to act or give up; end the rollout only if it stalls again
spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py:112-126: on an empty (no-tool) turn, if cfg.stop_on_empty_turn or nudged -> stop_reason='empty_turn' and break; otherwise append a single nudge USER message and set nudged=True. A second consecutive empty turn (nudged already True) breaks. nudged reset to False on any tool turn (loop.py:127).
spec_features.notes: Both branches enforced: first empty turn nudges, second empty turn ends the rollout. Default stop_on_empty_turn=False (loop.py:42).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If True, a no-tool-call assistant turn ends the rollout (treated as the model stalling). If False, we nudge it once and continue.

spec_features.evidence: runner/loop.py:87 `for turn in range(cfg.turn_budget)` bounds the loop. cfg default 25 (loop.py:35); per-task budgets set in tasks/registry.py:143,157,171,185,200 (25/30/30/25/35); override via configs/loader.py:53 and eval.py:101-109 falls back to task.turn_budget when <=0.
spec_features.notes: Enforced cap that terminates the loop; default stop_reason='budget'. Fully wired and overridable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reproducibility & cost knobs live in RolloutConfig. (loop.py:8); DESIGN names it the cost/signal knob but code carries no welfare reason

code_only_features.evidence: runner/loop.py:44 wall_time_cap_s: float = 0.0; loop.py:88-90 `if cfg.wall_time_cap_s and (time.time() - start) > cfg.wall_time_cap_s: stop_reason='wall_time'; break`. Read and acted on (breaks loop) when set; configurable via loader.py:58 / eval.py:108.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Hard cap on total wall time per rollout (seconds); 0 = no cap.
